question: How few unit fractions can add up to an ordinary fraction?
idea: A unit fraction has numerator one, such as one-third. The claim says every positive fraction below one can be written as a short sum of distinct unit fractions. The worst-case number of terms grows only like the logarithm of the logarithm of the original denominator, up to constants.
why: The study of whole numbers, primes, and equations. A simple question about numbers can hide an extremely difficult pattern.

glossary.meaning: A rational number is a number that can be written as a fraction of two integers.
A mathematical statement proposed to be true but requiring proof or a counterexample.

exactClaim: Every rational $a/b$ with $1\le a\lt b$ is a sum of $O(\log\log b)$ distinct positive unit fractions. The worst-case minimum number of terms has the same order, resolving Erdős’s conjecture on short Egyptian fractions. )
